title: packet_types color_rgba element type never checked (!ok typo for !okc) — malformed element silently coerced to 0
detail: `ok` is the outer `v.(json.Object)` assertion (always true here), so the element-type check is dead and `okc` is never consulted. Verified by execution at 37f5581: color_rgba [90,"oops",112,255] and [90,1.5,112,255] both load ACCEPTED with the element silently 0 — a silent default on malformed JSON, contra the ODN-5 fail-fast mandate.
recommended_fix: Change `if !ok || n < 0 || n > 255` to `if !okc || n < 0 || n > 255` so a non-integer color_rgba element fails fast with the named error.

title: Packet_Type.demand_weight has no range validation — negative weight loads silently (sibling fields are validated)
detail: The validation chain omits demand_weight, unlike Node_Type ("demand_weight must be >= 0", line 235) and Demand_Entry (de2.demand_weight < 1 rejected, line 358). Verified: email demand_weight=-7 loads ACCEPTED. A nonsense negative sibling weight reaches the 3.2/3.3 consumers unvalidated — an ODN-5 out-of-range gap.
recommended_fix: Add `pt.demand_weight < 1` (or `< 0`) to the packet_types validation chain, matching the Demand_Entry/Node_Type precedent, so a bad weight fails fast at load.

title: jint silently truncates json.Float — non-integer sim values accepted on the new 3.1 demand/packet fields
detail: The new 3.1 loaders read sim values via jint (e.g. line 355 `de2.volume = jint(eeo, "volume", 0)`). Verified: demand.json `"volume": 2.9` loads ACCEPTED as 2. The helper is carry-forward from 1.2, but its float truncation now silently admits non-integer sim values into the new catalogs, weakening the integer-only ODN-5/ODN-10 bar.
recommended_fix: For the new 3.1 sim fields, reject json.Float (fail fast) instead of truncating — e.g. a strict jint variant that errors when the value is not json.Integer.

title: weighted_pick comment claims zero/negative weights 'still count toward the total' — the code excludes them
detail: The comment says a zero/negative weight 'still counts toward the total', but `if w > 0 { total += u64(w) }` excludes it. The code is correct (counting it would let the draw overshoot acc and fail the pick); the comment misdescribes the load-bearing [E10] pick math.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment to 'a zero/negative weight is never picked and is excluded from the total' to match the implementation.

title: run_demo prints NUL-garbage for T2 failures — check_golden's temp-allocated messages are freed by the per-tick free_all before the print loop
detail: check_golden appends fmt.tprintf messages (temp allocator, goldens.odin:109) into fails inside the tick loop; free_all(context.temp_allocator) at each tick end frees them, so the FAIL print loop emits NUL bytes (observed running `harness run qos` at 37f5581: two blank lines for the two capture mismatches). Failure detail (mismatch count, diff path) is unreadable exactly when T2 fails.
recommended_fix: Allocate fails (or the check_golden messages) with context.allocator instead of the temp allocator, or defer free_all until after the failure report is printed/written.
